title: Jeff Heath (CEO, Freeform · Boise) — 'The obligation is to still be a place where decisions get made locally, where people are known by name, and where there's still a truck on the floor for the kids'
summary: Jeff Heath — second-generation CEO of Freeform, a locally-owned office-furnishings dealer in Boise — publishes a heartfelt reflection tagged 'Eric Ries' about his son finding the same Haworth truck he pushed around the office as a kid. Writes about how most family-owned dealers in his industry have sold to PE roll-ups or public companies, and what a company owes the place it comes from. 81 likes.
blockquote: Most of the family-owned dealers I grew up around have changed too. Sold to a public company, a private equity fund, a national roll-up. Of the dealers in Boise today, two are still locally owned, and we're one of them. That's not a complaint. A lot of those sales were good outcomes for good people. But it means the question of what a company is for mostly gets answered somewhere else now.
